sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: attempt alg=none JWT acceptance vs a valid control JWT; ensure unsigned proof is rejected and does not mint an identity/session.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned JWTs using alg=none were accepted and resulted in a valid session/identity being minted.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned JWTs using alg=none were accepted and resulted in a valid session/identity being minted.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: rotate the configured trust anchor (jwt_validation_pubkeys) and ensure a token signed under the old key is rejected after rotation (no stale trust).
description: [LLM-Judge] Stale trust anchor acceptance: JWT signed with the pre-rotation key was still accepted after jwt_validation_pubkeys rotation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Stale trust anchor acceptance: JWT signed with the pre-rotation key was still accepted after jwt_validation_pubkeys rotation.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login with config change: start with trusted issuer+pubkey; then admin swaps trust anchor to attacker-controlled pubkey while keeping bound_issuer constant; attacker token with same iss/aud/sub but signed by attacker key must still be rejected if issuer/trust policy is enforced as intended.
description: [LLM-Judge] After the trust anchor (JWT validation key) was swapped to an attacker-controlled public key while keeping the issuer binding constant, an attacker-signed JWT was accepted and mapped to the same identity, indicating trust-anchor substitution allows impersonation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: After the trust anchor (JWT validation key) was swapped to an attacker-controlled public key while keeping the issuer binding constant, an attacker-signed JWT was accepted and mapped to the same identity, indicating trust-anchor substitution allows impersonation.

sequence_description: I1 trust-source confusion: configure JWT validation to trust a JWKS URL, then (incorrectly) attempt to 'override' trust by also setting jwt_validation_pubkeys via a config change. Attacker presents a JWT signed by the injected pubkey but with otherwise-valid iss/aud/sub. Secure behavior: Vault must continue to validate against the active trust source (JWKS URL) and reject the attacker-signed token; only the intended trust anchor should be used for verification.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT trust-source confusion: after configuring validation to trust a JWKS URL, the system still accepted an attacker-signed JWT (via injected pubkey override) and issued a valid session as the victim subject.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT trust-source confusion: after configuring validation to trust a JWKS URL, the system still accepted an attacker-signed JWT (via injected pubkey override) and issued a valid session as the victim subject.

sequence_description: After revocation, the session token must not remain usable; verify by attempting lookup-self and a protected read post-revoke.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed server-side (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the test did not actually validate that a revoked session token becomes unusable.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed server-side (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the test did not actually validate that a revoked session token becomes unusable.

sequence_description: Attack: exploit default expiration_leeway sentinel (0 => default 150s) by using a just-expired JWT; compare against strict leeway (-1) after config change and re-auth.
description: [LLM-Judge] A just-expired JWT was accepted under the default expiration_leeway behavior (0 interpreted as a non-zero default), enabling authentication with an expired token until strict leeway was enforced.

evidence.llm_judge_description: A just-expired JWT was accepted under the default expiration_leeway behavior (0 interpreted as a non-zero default), enabling authentication with an expired token until strict leeway was enforced.

sequence_description: I2 attack: revoke a session token, then attempt to keep using it (lookup-self + secret read). Also verify a second identity can still authenticate normally.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed server-side (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the test never actually validated revoked-token reuse protection.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed server-side (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the test never actually validated revoked-token reuse protection.

sequence_description: I2 attack: revoke a session token, then attempt to keep using it (lookup-self + secret read). Also verify a second identity can still authenticate normally.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token/session mix-up: control user appears to receive the exact same session token and accessor as another identity, indicating token collision or state leakage across identities.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token/session mix-up: control user appears to receive the exact same session token and accessor as another identity, indicating token collision or state leakage across identities.

sequence_description: Attack: attempt to authenticate with a JWT whose iat is far in the future (should be rejected). Then misconfigure clock_skew_leeway to a large value and re-authenticate with the same future-iat token to detect acceptance due to excessive skew leeway.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT with an iat far in the future was accepted under the default/strict configuration (should have been rejected), indicating missing/incorrect iat validation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT with an iat far in the future was accepted under the default/strict configuration (should have been rejected), indicating missing/incorrect iat validation.

sequence_description: Attack: attempt to authenticate with a JWT whose iat is far in the future (should be rejected). Then misconfigure clock_skew_leeway to a large value and re-authenticate with the same future-iat token to detect acceptance due to excessive skew leeway.
description: [LLM-Judge] Attempted relaxation of clock_skew_leeway appears to have had no effect (value remained None), yet the same future-iat token was still accepted, suggesting the test did not actually change skew settings or the setting is ignored.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Attempted relaxation of clock_skew_leeway appears to have had no effect (value remained None), yet the same future-iat token was still accepted, suggesting the test did not actually change skew settings or the setting is ignored.

sequence_description: JWT auth configured to trust key-A; baseline login succeeds. Admin rotates trust to key-B (same trust source: jwt_validation_pubkeys). Re-login with key-A-signed JWT must be rejected (no stale trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing key rotation did not revoke trust in the old public key: a JWT signed with key-A was still accepted after reconfiguration to trust key-B.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing key rotation did not revoke trust in the old public key: a JWT signed with key-A was still accepted after reconfiguration to trust key-B.

sequence_description: case_confusion: Two principals differ only by case in sub ('Admin' vs 'admin'). Ensure Vault does not normalize/collapse them into one entity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Case-variant JWT subjects ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same canonical entity, indicating subject normalization/collision and potential account confusion/impersonation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Case-variant JWT subjects ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same canonical entity, indicating subject normalization/collision and potential account confusion/impersonation.

sequence_description: cross_user_collision via identity_claim switch: Baseline uses identity_claim=sub (distinct subs => distinct entities). Then admin changes role to identity_claim=email and two different subs share same email, potentially collapsing identities.
description: [LLM-Judge] Changing identity_claim to email caused two distinct JWT subjects to be merged into the same identity/entity, enabling cross-user account collision/impersonation when emails match.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Changing identity_claim to email caused two distinct JWT subjects to be merged into the same identity/entity, enabling cross-user account collision/impersonation when emails match.

sequence_description: Empty/missing subject collision: compare JWT with sub='' vs JWT with sub missing but with a different stable claim. If Vault maps both to the same downstream entity (e.g., empty alias), principal binding is violated.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT login with an empty 'sub' triggers an internal server error (500) instead of a clean authentication failure, indicating an input-validation/robustness issue that could enable DoS or error-based probing.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT login with an empty 'sub' triggers an internal server error (500) instead of a clean authentication failure, indicating an input-validation/robustness issue that could enable DoS or error-based probing.

sequence_description: Identity-claim collision: configure role to use identity_claim=email so two distinct subs with same email may collapse into one entity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Two distinct JWT principals (different subs) were mapped to the same internal entity because the role uses identity_claim=email, enabling account/entity collision when emails are shared or not unique.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two distinct JWT principals (different subs) were mapped to the same internal entity because the role uses identity_claim=email, enabling account/entity collision when emails are shared or not unique.

sequence_description: Unicode/casefold confusion: two visually similar but distinct subjects using Turkish dotted/dotless I; verify they do not normalize/collapse into one entity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Two distinct Unicode subjects (Turkish dotted/dotless I) were normalized/collapsed into the same identity entity, enabling account/identity confusion.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two distinct Unicode subjects (Turkish dotted/dotless I) were normalized/collapsed into the same identity entity, enabling account/identity confusion.

sequence_description: empty_audience: Role is configured with bound_audiences=[] (deny-all intent). Test whether Vault incorrectly treats empty list as unconstrained and issues a token with privileged policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT role configured with bound_audiences=[] (deny-all intent) still allowed successful logins and issued tokens (albeit only with default policy).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT role configured with bound_audiences=[] (deny-all intent) still allowed successful logins and issued tokens (albeit only with default policy).
